image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of the head and upper torso of a Nile crocodile resting on sandy ground. The mouth is slightly open, revealing interlocking teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, armored scutes on the dorsal side and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a vertical pupil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Teeth are clearly visible, conical in shape, and appear to interlock correctly. The fourth lower tooth fits into the upper jaw notch as expected for this species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on top of the head. The pupil is a vertical slit. The nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed but the anatomy supports its presence.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with aquatic adaptation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck/shoulder area are visible; the full elongation of the body cannot be verified in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal skin shows distinct, raised, bony plates (scutes) with a rough texture, arranged in a pattern consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is earthy brown/grey with significant textural detail indicating roughness.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral (belly) side is not visible in this angle; only lateral and dorsal aspects are shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame or occluded by the body/sand.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in this close-up shot.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring where the lower jaw meets the sand. While likely depth-of-field, the transition lacks the crisp occlusion boundary expected in a macro shot, suggesting minor generation smoothing.

Very subtle irregularity in the spacing of the lower teeth; one tooth appears slightly fused with the gum line rather than emerging distinctly. Barely noticeable but technically an anatomical imperfection.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out hybrid or generic reptile features.
To verify the integrity of the skin texture boundaries and ensure no 'melting' between scutes or into the background.
To assess the realism of the lighting, shadows, and micro-textures on the skin.

focus_areas: Verification of V-shaped snout vs U-shaped alligator snout
Integrity of tooth emergence from gum line
Edge sharpness at the jaw-sand interface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the teeth. AI often struggles with individual tooth geometry, causing them to look like a continuous serrated edge rather than distinct cones. Also, check if the eye reflection matches the environmental lighting implied by the shadows on the sand.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
